full_judgment:
Ruhul Islam, J: This petition for Special Leave to Appeal by the defendants is directed against the judgment and decree dated January 30, 1979 passed by the High Court Division in First Appeal No.198 of 1965 dismissing the appeal and affirming the judgment and decree of the Trial Court decreeing the suit for declaration of title and recovery of khas possession. 

 The Respondents 1 and 2 instituted Title Suit No.26 of 1959 in the Third Court of Subordinate Judge, Dacca stating, inter-alia, that the land measuring 1.16 acres in C.S. Plot No.160 of Mouza Dhammandi belionged to Atibal Peshi. Jagrup Peshi being the sole heir after the death of Atibal Peshi inherited the same and transferred 82 1/2 acres to Kamakshya Charan Bandopadhya by a kabala dated February 6, 1928. The transfer was confirmed by the landlord Nasiruddin Khan, Mutwalli of the Waqf estate by accepting a registered lease dated February 8, 1928. Jagrup Peshi also transferred 161/2 acres of land from south-estern portion of the plot to Kamakshya Charan Bandopadhya by another kabala dated 18th Magh, 1338 corresponding to 1st February 1932. He further transferred 10 Kathas of land to Sachindra Charan Gupta by another kabala dated 27th of Magh 1331 B.S. corresponding to 9th February 1925. Kamakshya Charan purchased the interest of Sachindra Charan Gupta by a kabala dated 3rd Magh, 1943 B.S. corresponding to 16th January, 1937.  Kamakha Charan Bandapadhya thus became the owner of 31/2 bighas of land and possessed the same on payment of rent to the landlord. After partition in 1947 Kamakshya Charan settled in West Bengal and he sold the land to the plaintiff No.1 by kabala dated 4th March, 1955 who held the same as raiyati joti and was in khas possession thereof. In a Rent Sale at the instance of a landlord against Kamakshya the suit land was auction sold and it was purchased by one Hafizur Rahman and the plaintiff No.1 obtained another kabala from the auction purchased on 4.3.1955. Thereafter the plaintiff No.1 executed a khai Khalashi in favour of plaintiff No.2 for a period of 2 years. Defendants No.11 and 12 erected a small building on the suit land in the absence of the plaintiffs, the defendants also resisted the promethean of plaintiffs of March 1956 then denied the title of the plaintiffs on 21st December, 1956.
